metadata.doc: Node represents any architectural entity in the codebase (package, file, type, function, interface, table).
Edge represents a directed architectural relationship between two nodes.
Graph represents the complete or partial architectural graph of a codebase.
New creates an empty Graph.
AddNode adds a node to the graph if it doesn't already exist.
AddEdge adds an edge to the graph. Silently skips duplicates (same From, To, Kind).
NodeByID finds a node by its unique ID.

NeighborsOf returns a one-hop subgraph containing the target node,
all immediately connected nodes (incoming and outgoing), and all incident edges between them.
NodesByFile returns all nodes belonging to a specific file path.
NodesByPackage returns all nodes belonging to a specific package name.
ToJSON serializes the Graph into pretty-printed JSON bytes.
FromJSON deserializes JSON bytes into a Graph.
Analyzer represents a language-agnostic static analyzer interface.
Analyzer implements static analysis for Go codebases.
New creates a new Go static analyzer.
Analyze statically inspects a Go repository at repoPath and returns an architectural Graph.

extractDecls walks top-level declarations in a file and adds type, interface,
and function nodes along with their containment edges.

receiverTypeName extracts the base type name from a receiver expression,
handling both value receivers (T) and pointer receivers (*T).

extractCalls resolves function call expressions to their callee declarations
using the type checker info and emits directed "calls" edges.

typeToNamed unwraps a pointer and returns the underlying named type's name,
or the empty string if the type is not a named type.

extractImplementationsAndReferences emits "implements" edges (struct → interface)
and "references" edges (struct → field type) for all local named types.

LLMClient is the language-model abstraction used by the server.
Implementations live in llm/ollama, llm/openai, and llm/anthropic.

Explain generates a layered architectural explanation for a single node,
using the node's source code and its immediate subgraph as context.
Client calls any OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint.
Options configures the OpenAI-compatible client.
New creates a new OpenAI-compatible LLM client.
Explain generates a layered architectural explanation for the given node.
writeJSON encodes v as JSON and writes it to w with the given status code.
writeError writes a { "error": "..." } JSON body with the given status code.

handleGraph returns the full graph as JSON.

	Response: graph.Graph

handleNode dispatches between single-node and neighbors requests based on
whether the path ends with "/neighbors".

	GET /api/node/:id           → graph.Node
	GET /api/node/:id/neighbors → { nodes: []Node, edges: []Edge }
explainRequest is the JSON body for the explain endpoint.

formatNodeAsSourceHint produces a human-readable summary of a node's metadata
to substitute for real source code until disk-reading is implemented.
Server wraps an HTTP server with all its dependencies.
Options configures a Server instance.
New creates a configured Server and registers all routes.

ServeHTTP implements http.Handler, allowing the Server to be used directly
in tests with httptest.NewRecorder without binding to a real port.
Start begins listening. It blocks until the context is cancelled.
loggingMiddleware logs every request when verbose is true.

corsMiddleware adds permissive CORS headers for local development.
The UI dev server runs on a different port from the Go server, so these
are required during development. In production the Go server also serves
the UI, making CORS irrelevant, but the headers are harmless.

spaHandler wraps a file server to support single-page applications.
If the requested path doesn't correspond to an existing file, it serves
index.html so that client-side routing can take over.

openBrowser launches the default browser at url.
Failures are non-fatal — the user can always open the URL manually.
buildLLMClient selects and constructs an LLM client based on the provider flag.
loadGraph either reads a valid cache or re-runs the analyzer.

tryReadCache returns the cached graph if the cache file is newer than any
.go source file in the repo. Returns (nil, false) on any miss or error.
writeCache serialises the graph to the cache file, creating parent dirs.
